text:
miriam: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a small, backwards-compatible extension to the policy DSL: add a hedged_routing strategy and a regional_cost_cap field. want to capture tradeoffs and rollout plan here.

alex: high level — hedged_routing = send parallel requests to two candidate pools and accept the faster response? how do we avoid double-cost explosions? :thinking_face:

miriam: yes, hedged_routing = target low-latency SLOs by duplicating only when latency risk is high. we control duplication with dynamic tokens and a cost cap. main knobs: replicas, trigger_latency_ms, max_additional_cost_pct, and regional_cost_cap to bound spend per region.

sahil: question on interface: should hedged_routing be a top-level strategy or a modifier you can attach to any strategy? prefer modifier so e.g. "strategy: best_cost" + "hedge: { replicas:2 }" keeps adapter complexity lower.

jess: backwards-compat note: if we add top-level fields, older clients might ignore them safely, but runtime should validate and reject invalid combos (e.g., hedge + batch_all). need clear error messages.

miriam: agreed on modifier approach. sample YAML DSL (rough):

```yaml
route: /v1/generate
match: tenant == \"standard\"
strategy: best_cost
modifiers:
  hedging:
    enabled: true
    replicas: 2
    trigger_ms: 60  # trigger extra replica after this latency
    max_additional_cost_pct: 30
  regional_cost_cap: 0.15  # per-region, $ per 1k tokens
```

sam: rollout checklist: 1) telemetry hooks (count hedged requests, cost increment, p50/p95 delta), 2) canary with synthetic latency injection, 3) soft-fail path where hedging is a suggestion and runtime can drop it if budget exceeded.

alex: telemetry details: we should emit metric labels: hedged=true/false, hedge_origin(pool id), extra_cost_estimate, and hedge_outcome (served_by_primary / served_by_replica / both). these will let Optimize recommend configs.

miriam: for budget enforcement: two layers — pre-check (regional_cost_cap denies applying hedge if estimated cost > cap) and post-accounting (chargebacks and alerts if we overshot). pre-check needs quick estimate: cost_est = expected_tokens * cost_per_token(candidate). we have recent perf table for cost_per_token per model/region.

sahil: what about stateful fallbacks — if replica loses KV cache and becomes much slower, hedging might worsen latency. we should add a quick health score check (cache_hot boolean + recent_latency_ms) before selecting replica.

jess: API compatibility: clients can opt-in via policy flag. default off. also we should add feature-flag gate in control plane + CLI rollout (beta flag) so product experiments can enable per-tenant.

miriam: perf/ops concern: extra replicas create head-of-line effects on shared pools. propose runtime limits: global_hedge_qps and per-pool_hedge_ratio. if limits reached, runtime converts hedging request to non-hedged fallthrough or reduces replicas.

sam: testing: unit tests for policy parser, integration test with synthetic models that sleep, e2e canary that injects 100ms latency on primary and verify hedged path saves p95.

infra-bot: deploy queued: policy-dsl/hedging-prototype -> staging (sha: abc123) by miriam at 2026-03-20T15:22:10Z

miriam: next steps: I'll open a short RFC addendum with the modifier schema, validation rules, rollout plan, and telemetry proto. tagging folks for review @alex @sahil @jess. please comment on the DSL snippet and any missing safety knobs. :thumbsup:
